key_insight: This paper unifies several transfer learning settings into a single view for domains that evolve over time, instead of treating them as separate problems. It highlights that the best transfer strategy depends on how the target domain changes and how much labeled data is available when training happens.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the fragmentation of transfer learning research into isolated sub-areas like domain generalisation, domain adaptation, and multi-domain learning. It tackles the practical challenge of learning models that remain effective when the target domain is changing and training data availability is uncertain.
method: Reframes transfer learning settings under a common framework centered on evolving domains.
Analyzes how source and target domain relationships change under different data and label availability assumptions.
Connects existing transfer learning paradigms to show when each is appropriate in real-world evolving scenarios.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a clearer way to choose or design transfer learning methods for non-stationary environments. It is especially useful for applications where data drift, shifting labels, or delayed annotation make standard assumptions unrealistic.
visual_elements: A timeline showing domain evolution over time from source to target.
A taxonomy diagram linking domain generalisation, domain adaptation, and multi-domain learning.
A matrix comparing label availability vs. target data availability across settings.
An icon-based pipeline illustrating knowledge transfer from multiple sources to an evolving target domain.
paper_authors: Ricardo Ribeiro Pereira, Jacopo Bono, Hugo Ferreira, Pedro Ribeiro, Pedro Saleiro
